_comment: Colour slide films from the makers' product information bulletins, read off the vector graphs (pdf.js; axes from the grid lines, the tick values read off the rendered page). char: Status A density per layer (R = red-sensitive / cyan dye, G / magenta, B / yellow) vs log10 exposure in lux-seconds, daylight. sens: log10 relative spectral sensitivity per layer (1/exposure for a density 1.0 above D-min), drawn by the maker down to about -0.7. dye: spectral diffuse density of each dye, each normalised to a peak of 1. negatives: colour negative films (Status M curves, sensitivities, the published D-min and midscale-neutral spectra; the three dyes' shapes, which Kodak doesn't publish for still films, from a sister motion-picture negative, checked against the film's own neutral spectrum). papers: colour printing papers (Status A curves, log sensitivities, the three dyes in reflection).

films.src: Fujifilm FUJICHROME Velvia 100 Professional [RVP100], product information bulletin AF3-202E, p. 8 (E-6, Status A)
Fujifilm FUJICHROME Astia 100F Professional [RAP100F], data sheet AF3-149E, p. 8 (E-6, Status A)
Fujifilm FUJICHROME Provia 400F Professional [RHP III], data sheet AF3-066E, p. 6 (E-6, Status A; below D 1.0 the three curves are drawn as one)
Fujifilm FUJICHROME PROVIA 400X Professional [RXP], data sheet AF3-0213E, p. 7 (E-6, Status A; curves told apart by the legend: R solid, G dash-dot, B dotted)

Fujifilm FUJICHROME T64 Professional [RTP], data sheet AF3-178E, p. 7 (E-6, Status A; curves told apart by the legend). A tungsten-balanced film: its blue layer is ~6x more sensitive than its red; rendered as if shot under its own tungsten light (the white balance has neutralised the scene light), not with the blue cast it gets in daylight.

negatives.src: Kodak Professional Portra 400, publication E-4050 (2016), p. 4: characteristic curves (Status M, daylight), spectral sensitivities, D-min and midscale-neutral spectra
negatives.dyeSrc: Dye shapes: Kodak Vision3 250D colour negative (ECN-2, 2016 brochure p. 3, peak-normalised) — Kodak publishes no separate dye curves for Portra; their fit to Portra's own midscale-neutral spectrum is the check.

negatives.src: Fujifilm FUJICOLOR SUPERIA X-TRA 400 [CH], data sheet AF3-151E, p. 6: characteristic curves (Status M, daylight), spectral sensitivities, D-min and mid-scale-neutral spectra. Fuji's fourth, cyan-sensitive layer (it holds back the red-sensitive layer) is not modelled.
negatives.dyeSrc: Dye shapes: Kodak Vision3 250D colour negative (ECN-2, 2016 brochure p. 3, peak-normalised), as for Portra: Fujifilm publishes no separate dye curves for Superia; they rebuild Superia's own mid-scale-neutral spectrum to RMS 0.098 density (Fuji's yellow and magenta dyes peak about 12 nm further red than Kodak's).

papers.src: Kodak Professional Portra Endura paper, publication E-4021 (2003), pp. 9-10: characteristic curves (Status A, RA-4), spectral sensitivities, spectral dye densities

Kodak Professional Supra Endura paper, publication E-4021 (2003), p. 9: characteristic curves (Status A, RA-4); p. 10: spectral sensitivities and spectral dye densities (one set for Portra and Supra Endura)
